events.title: Hezbollah fires on Israel after US-Israeli strikes on Iran; Israel hits Beirut
events.detail: Hezbollah launched rockets and drones at northern Israel, its first claimed attack since the November 2024 ceasefire, after the US-Israeli war on Iran and the killing of Ali Khamenei. The IDF said it began striking Hezbollah targets across Lebanon, including Beirut, and ordered evacuations of dozens of villages in the south and Bekaa. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported dozens killed on day one (figures vary by source, 31–52).

events.title: Lebanese government bans Hezbollah military activity
events.detail: PM Nawaf Salam's government outlawed Hezbollah's military activities and demanded the group surrender its arms, a historic break with the movement. State media were later told to stop calling Hezbollah 'the resistance'. On 5 March the government also announced arrests/expulsions of anyone linked to Iran's IRGC.

events.title: Evacuation notices for Beirut's southern suburbs; Ghazali family strike in Mashghara
events.detail: Israel issued evacuation warnings for Dahiyeh. An airstrike on the Ghazali home in Mashghara during iftar killed four including two children; the IDF said the father served in a Hezbollah anti-tank unit. UNIFIL counted 210+ Hezbollah missiles fired since 2 March. Health Ministry toll: 102 killed, 638 wounded.

events.title: Israel strikes ten Beirut high-rises; Ghanaian UNIFIL HQ hit
events.detail: The IDF struck Hezbollah headquarters in ten high-rise buildings in Beirut. Two Israeli strikes/tank rounds hit the Ghanaian UNIFIL battalion headquarters, wounding peacekeepers. Cumulative ministry toll reached 217 killed, 798 wounded.

events.title: Nabi Chit strikes kill 41 after Israeli raid for Ron Arad
events.detail: Following an Israeli raid near Nabi Chit (Bekaa) reportedly searching for missing airman Ron Arad, airstrikes killed more than 40 people including Lebanese soldiers and a General Security member. Toll: 294 killed, 1,023 wounded.

events.title: Strike on Beirut hotel kills Quds Force officers; first IDF fatalities
events.detail: An Israeli strike on a Beirut hotel killed four (IDF later said five senior Quds Force/Hezbollah commanders). Two IDF soldiers were killed when a Hezbollah rocket hit their vehicle. Netanyahu warned that those who do not lay down arms would have their blood spilled.

events.title: Lebanese parliament postpones elections to 2028
events.detail: Parliament postponed the May 2026 legislative elections to May 2028 citing the war. Same day: ministry toll 486 killed, 1,313 wounded; an Israeli tank round killed a Catholic priest in Al-Qlayaa.

events.title: Toll passes 570; ~760,000 registered displaced
events.detail: The Health Ministry reported 570 killed (439 men, 45 women, 86 children, 14 health workers) and 1,444 wounded; nearly 760,000 people were registered as displaced within the first nine days.

events.title: Medics killed at Burj Qalaouiyah; Zrarieh bridge destroyed
events.detail: A strike on a health facility in Burj Qalaouiyah killed 12 medics. Israel destroyed the Zrarieh bridge over the Litani, the first of several bridges cut to isolate the south. Toll: 773 killed, 1,933 wounded.

events.title: Hezbollah cluster munition hits Metula; 31 paramedics among dead
events.detail: Ministry toll 826 killed, 2,009 wounded including 31 paramedics. Hezbollah fired a cluster munition at Metula.

era: Ground Invasion and Escalation (16 Mar–15 Apr 2026)

events.title: Israel announces ground operations in southern Lebanon
events.detail: Defence Minister Israel Katz announced a ground operation; the IDF's 91st Division began limited operations against Hezbollah strongholds to strengthen a forward defence zone. Katz said displaced residents would not return south of the Litani until northern Israel was secure.

events.title: Katz: IDF to hold security control up to the Litani
events.detail: Katz said Israel would keep security control up to the Litani River and demolish border-village houses on a Gaza model. On 31 March he said forces would hold the whole border-to-Litani area after the offensive; PM Salam warned the UN of annexation risk.

events.title: Hezbollah's most intense day: 105 attack waves
events.detail: Hezbollah launched 105 attack waves at Israeli targets, the peak of its fire at that point per the Alma Center (an Israeli think tank). A rocket barrage on 24 March killed a woman in northern Israel; on 26 March rockets killed a man in Nahariya.

events.title: Al-Manar and Al-Mayadeen journalists killed in Israeli strike
events.detail: An Israeli strike killed an Al-Manar journalist and two Al-Mayadeen journalists in south Lebanon. Israel typically alleges Hezbollah affiliation for staff of both outlets; press-freedom groups dispute blanket targeting claims.

events.title: Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeepers killed in two incidents
events.detail: One Indonesian peacekeeper was killed on 29 March near Adchit al-Qusayr by a projectile of unknown origin and two more on 30 March near Bani Hayyan in an explosion. UN Secretary-General Guterres said attacks on peacekeepers may amount to war crimes; UNIFIL opened investigations. The UN later said the 30 March deaths were likely caused by a Hezbollah-planted explosive.

events.title: Lebanon toll above 1,200; 1.1M displaced by month's end
events.detail: The ministry toll passed 1,000 on 19 March and reached ~1,238 by 29 March. By the end of March more than 1.1 million people, nearly one-fifth of the population, had been displaced. IDF said it killed Hezbollah southern front commander Yusuf Ismail Hashem on 31 March.

events.title: Strikes widen to Hezbollah finance and border crossings
events.detail: The IDF struck two currency-exchange shops in Beirut (continuing a campaign on Al-Qard Al-Hasan branches, money changers and fuel stations aimed at Hezbollah's ~$700M/year funding) and on 4 April ordered evacuation of the Masnaa crossing. Ministry toll 1,318 on 1 April, 1,422 by 4 April.

events.title: Israel's largest strikes of the war after Iran ceasefire
events.detail: After the US–Israel–Iran ceasefire, Netanyahu said it did not cover Lebanon. The IDF struck over 100 Hezbollah targets, with Al Jazeera reporting at least 254 killed and 92 in Beirut in one wave. Hezbollah said it halted attacks.

events.title: Nabatieh strike kills 19 incl. 13 State Security personnel
events.detail: An Israeli strike in Nabatieh killed 19, including 13 Lebanese State Security personnel. Hezbollah fired a missile at Ashdod and rockets damaged a historic church in Nahariya. Toll hit 2,020 on 11 April.

events.title: First direct Israel–Lebanon talks in Washington since 1993
events.detail: Ambassadors Yechiel Leiter (Israel) and Nada Hamadeh Moawad (Lebanon) met with Secretary of State Rubio in Washington, the first such talks in decades.

events.title: Israel destroys Qasmieh Bridge on truce day
events.detail: Israel destroyed the Qasmieh Bridge near Tyre as the truce was announced; Reuters toll 2,294 by 17 April.

events.title: Trump announces 10-day Israel–Lebanon ceasefire
events.detail: Trump announced a 10-day truce effective 5 p.m. ET. The State Department text has both states declaring they are not at war, committing to US-facilitated direct talks, and requiring Lebanon to act against Hezbollah attacks. Hezbollah was not a party; coverage was unclear on whether it was bound. Strikes continued, including a Tyre strike that killed 13 of one family.

events.title: French UNIFIL soldiers killed in Deir Kifa
events.detail: A French peacekeeper was killed on 18 April and a second died of wounds on 22 April. Macron blamed Hezbollah, which denied responsibility. UNIFIL reports 7 peacekeepers killed in the war.

events.title: Trump announces three-week extension after White House meeting
events.detail: Lebanon and Israel agreed to extend the ceasefire by three weeks after meeting at the White House. Violations were alleged by both sides; on 25 April Netanyahu ordered the IDF to 'vigorously strike' Hezbollah and from 27 April Israel struck eastern Lebanon again.

events.title: Qassem: Hezbollah will not revert to its pre-March status
events.detail: Hezbollah secretary-general Naim Qassem said the group would not return to its previous posture as Israel resumed strikes on the Bekaa. Evacuation orders covered 15 villages near Nabatieh on 30 April; a drone strike on Moshav Shomera injured 12 Israeli soldiers.

events.title: Truce extended another 45 days amid civil-defence strike
events.detail: Israel and Lebanon extended the truce 45 days. The same day a strike on a civil defence centre killed at least six, including three paramedics, and two IDF soldiers were killed. Ministry toll passed 3,000 on 18 May.

events.title: Ministry toll since 2 March passes 3,000
events.detail: The Health Ministry's cumulative toll reached 3,020 (2,988 on 17 May). Over 200 children had been killed by mid-May. IDF deaths in south Lebanon reached 21 on 19 May.

events.title: IDF crosses Litani, captures Beaufort Castle
events.detail: Katz ordered the army to expand operations, cross the Litani and take the Beaufort ridge. Israel announced capture of the 900-year-old castle, its deepest incursion in 26 years, despite the declared truce. Netanyahu called it a decisive turning point. France requested an emergency UN Security Council meeting.

events.title: Iran links Hormuz traffic to Lebanon truce
events.detail: Iran announced Hormuz open during the truce on 17 April and closed it again 18 April; the Lebanon front became a bargaining variable in US–Iran talks.

era: Peace Frameworks and Occupation (1 Jun–31 Aug 2026)

events.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to renew truce and plan 'pilot zones'
events.detail: A US-mediated agreement renewed the ceasefire and introduced 'pilot zones' for staged Israeli withdrawal. Hezbollah rejected the deal on 4 June, demanding full ceasefire and withdrawal; Speaker Nabih Berri proposed mutual withdrawal south of the Litani.

events.title: IDF orders evacuation of all of Tyre
events.detail: The IDF ordered Tyre evacuated; strikes killed eight in Tyre and four in Nabatieh. Ministry toll 3,666. Israel did not strike Beirut's southern suburbs after a 1 June US-proposed understanding, though strikes there resumed 7–14 June.

events.title: US–Iran announcement of end to operations covers Lebanon; Israel stays
events.detail: Pakistan, mediating, said the US and Iran declared an end to military operations on all fronts including Lebanon. Israel said its forces would remain in occupied areas. Trump said he planned to speak to Hezbollah; Israel objected to Lebanon's inclusion.

events.title: Trump announces renewed Israel–Hezbollah truce; deadliest day follows
events.detail: Trump announced a truce effective 4 p.m. local time; the ministry reported 47 killed that day and 83 on 20 June (toll 4,057). Four 401st Brigade soldiers including a lieutenant colonel died to an explosive drone at Kfar Tebnit. Iran re-closed Hormuz on 20 June citing Israeli strikes.

events.title: Israel–Lebanon framework agreement signed in Washington
events.detail: Ambassadors Leiter and Moawad signed a US framework 'first step' toward peace, creating a Military Coordination Group for Lebanon and $100M US humanitarian aid, tying Israeli withdrawal to Hezbollah disarmament via the Lebanese army. Hezbollah was not a party and opposed it; Netanyahu said Israel stays in its security zone.

events.title: Iran, US and Lebanon agree committee to oversee war's end
events.detail: Iran said Iran, the US and Lebanon agreed to form a committee overseeing the end of the war in Lebanon. Ministry toll 4,278.

events.title: Israel hands pilot zones to Lebanese army (Srifa, Froun, Zawtar)
events.detail: Israel withdrew from pilot zones in Srifa, Froun and, on 21 July, Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, where the Lebanese army deployed under the Military Coordination Group. Troops exchanged warning fire near Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh; residents' return remained blocked. Israel re-entered Zawtar on 8 August.

events.title: Israel and Lebanon agree shortlist of states to verify Hezbollah disarmament
events.detail: The two sides agreed on candidate states to verify disarmament. The US sanctioned Hezbollah on 20 August.

events.title: World Bank projects 6.4% contraction for Lebanon in 2026
events.detail: The World Bank forecast a 6.4% GDP contraction (vs. 4.2% growth estimated for 2025), inflation near 17.5% and $3.57B lost tourism/consumption; the finance minister expects a 7–10% contraction and up to $20B in damage.

events.title: US sanctions Hezbollah
events.detail: The US imposed new sanctions on Hezbollah on 20 August, per secondary compilation.

events.title: Strike on Kfar Reman residential building kills 12 of one family
events.detail: An Israeli strike killed 12 members of one family; Arabsalim evacuation ordered the same day. Ali al-Taher ridge control is disputed: Israel declared it part of its security zone on 3 September though an AP photographer found no IDF presence.

events.title: IDF detonates 1,000+ tons of explosives under Ali al-Taher ridge
events.detail: Netanyahu announced destruction of a Hezbollah complex beneath the ridge with over 1,000 tons of TNT. The 401st Brigade claimed 1,200 tunnels destroyed by 2 August; IDF said it completed dismantling facilities in al-Mansouri on 28 September.

events.title: Unexploded munition kills teenager in northern Israel; strikes continue
events.detail: A 15-year-old was killed and about two dozen hurt when a Hezbollah munition detonated near the border; Israeli strikes killed civilians in the south, including during the olive harvest. Lebanese authorities intercepted a truck with 780 kg of explosives. Lebanon–Israel military meetings are planned for 20 and 22 October.
